> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c5fb3efdf33a8e343442739e0ebeef1b1e47251` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6d5d3b2abc3c7486b0ee11288fa439ca5b3e7529` — the merge of head `eddb22176d7312fca17de3c4020eeb3bfeb53110` into base `9c5fb3efdf33a8e343442739e0ebeef1b1e47251`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6d5d3b2abc3c7486b0ee11288fa439ca5b3e7529 && git checkout 6d5d3b2abc3c7486b0ee11288fa439ca5b3e7529
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9c5fb3efdf33a8e343442739e0ebeef1b1e47251 eddb22176d7312fca17de3c4020eeb3bfeb53110 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9c5fb3efdf33a8e343442739e0ebeef1b1e47251 && git merge --no-ff eddb22176d7312fca17de3c4020eeb3bfeb53110

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c5fb3efdf33a8e343442739e0ebeef1b1e47251
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9c5fb3efdf33a8e343442739e0ebeef1b1e47251` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `79e98ffc3b84906df10f40c164317539b47fa636`

Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts + none (no file in the diff implements them); read outside the diff: packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.ts, packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.test.ts and packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts on `origin/main` fa7d94b64ee
Security-touching: yes

Full review of this head, claimed in 7145444800. Face: published schema (`packages/spec/src/**`, non-test). Read-only shape: the diff, card 36917, the dev report 7145362635 and the code the new sentences cite on `origin/main`. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The premise holds.** `ownerTransferOff(obj)` in `user-assigned-work.ts` is `isTransferEligible(obj) && !resolveUserActionTransfer(obj).enabled`, so the hand-over is a real second consumer of the switch and the old description was too narrow.
- **"Reads only on or off, not the predicates" is true.** The hand-over reads `.enabled` and never `predicates`.
- **"Counted as held and keep their owner" is true on an eligible object.** `userAssignedWorkFields` marks `owner_id` `transferable: false` with reason `transfer_off`, the count reports it, and `transferUserAssignedWork` filters on `transferable`.
- **"Gates the action and the hand-over's owner_id, not a plain owner_id write" is true.** Only `owner_id` takes the `transfer_off` reason; the object's other user fields are handed over whatever the switch says.
- **The `resolveUserActionTransfer` docblock is exact.** It says the hand-over holds "an eligible object's `owner_id` rows" where the resolution answers `enabled: false`, which is the code's conjunction.
- **Two of the new sentences drop that conjunction.** See M1.
- **The regenerated `object.mdx` row equals the `.describe()` string.** One row moved and nothing else.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec` `patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. Correct: no shape, accepted value or default moves. The semantic change itself shipped with the hand-over PR, and this is the description catching up.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev report has no `open_questions` entry. Its one out-of-scope note is N1 below.
- SQL push-down: no code changed.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- `Security-touching: yes` is the conservative value: the hunks describe who keeps record ownership at offboarding. No governed path is in this diff, so no arm reads the line, and it is not a request for a `security` label.
- Check-runs on this head were still in progress when this record was written. The verdict below does not rest on them.

### ④ Design judgment

- `object.zod.ts`: the `.describe()` is the sentence an author and an AI read, in the JSON schema and in the reference docs. Naming the hand-over there is the right place and the right size. The sentence is wrong on one class of object, which is M1.
- `user-action-transfer.ts`: the opening line and the "three readers" docblock hold against the code. The "The switch gates two consumers" paragraph has the same hole as the `.describe()`.

Findings:

- M1 (must-fix): open.
- N1 (nit): open.

M1. The hand-over holds `owner_id` only where the object is eligible and the switch resolves off. The new text says it holds wherever the switch is off. `resolveUserActionTransfer` answers `enabled: false` for every ineligible object, so on those the text and the code disagree:

- An object the platform gives no owner (`systemFields: false`, or `ownership` other than `user`) that declares its own `owner_id` user field: the switch resolves off, and the hand-over **moves** that `owner_id`. `user-assigned-work.test.ts` on main pins this ("an owner_id the platform does not provide is app-authored work: the switch does not govern it", a `controlled_by_parent` detail with `systemFields: false`). An author can write `transfer: false` there, and the new description tells them the owner is kept.
- An object that declares `owner_id` read-only: the hand-over skips read-only fields, so those rows are not counted at all, held or otherwise.

The three places that need the eligibility scope:

- The `.describe()` on `userActions.transfer`: "Also decides whether the offboarding hand-over … moves this object's owner_id: off, those records are counted as held and keep their owner".
- The module paragraph in `user-action-transfer.ts`: "Where it resolves off, the hand-over's count reports the object's `owner_id` rows as held (`transfer_off`) and its transfer leaves their owner where it is".
- The changeset: "where the switch resolves off, those records are counted as held and keep their owner". This sentence ships in `CHANGELOG.md`.

A wording that would hold, for the `.describe()`: "On those objects it also decides whether the offboarding hand-over of a user's assigned work moves owner_id: off, those records are counted as held and keep their owner (the hand-over reads only on or off, not the predicates). An owner_id the platform does not provide is handed over like any other user field." The module paragraph and the changeset take the same scope ("where an eligible object's switch resolves off"). Regenerate `object.mdx` after the edit.

N1. The TSDoc above `userActions` in `object.zod.ts` names the endpoint and the console as readers and not the hand-over. It is not false, it is outside the card's file surface, and the dev report already notes it. The fix round may add the third reader there or leave it.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36917-transfer-describe-offboarding`
Reviewed-by: `session_011y7As5bdhV5T4N9vpjmZzH`

Review run: an isolated one-shot sub-agent of the seat session, which ran no other agent; the seat adopts.

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · head 79e98ffc3b84906df10f40c164317539b47fa636

2026-11-24T21:52Z · L1 (one-shot reviewer), checked against GitHub and `origin/main` (fa7d94b64ee), not against the report's own account. Card #36917, claim 7144508786, dev report 7145362635, contract review 7145492854 (FAIL, same head).

**One must-fix, prose only.** The new text says the hand-over holds `owner_id` wherever the switch is off. The code holds it only on an eligible object: `ownerTransferOff` is `isTransferEligible(obj) && !resolveUserActionTransfer(obj).enabled`, and the resolver answers off for every ineligible object. On an object the platform gives no owner that declares its own `owner_id` user field, the switch resolves off and the hand-over moves that field. `user-assigned-work.test.ts` on main pins it ("an owner_id the platform does not provide is app-authored work: the switch does not govern it"). On an object with a read-only `owner_id` the rows are not counted at all.

Three sentences need the eligibility scope, then a regen of `object.mdx`:

- `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, the `userActions.transfer` `.describe()`: "Also decides whether the offboarding hand-over … moves this object's owner_id: off, those records are counted as held and keep their owner".
- `packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts`, the "The switch gates two consumers" paragraph: "Where it resolves off, the hand-over's count reports the object's `owner_id` rows as held".
- `.changeset/36917-transfer-describe-offboarding.md`: "where the switch resolves off, those records are counted as held and keep their owner".

Contract review 7145492854 carries a wording that holds. The `resolveUserActionTransfer` docblock already says "an eligible object's `owner_id` rows" and needs no change.

### Checklist

1. **PR shape:** draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36917`. `Fixes` is right once the must-fix is closed: the card asks for the `.describe()` and the module text, and both are in the diff. No closing keyword sits next to another card number.
2. **Scope:** 4 files, +28/−10: the two claimed spec files, the regenerated `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` and one changeset. Nothing under `content/docs/releases/`, no codegen script, nothing outside the claim's file surface.
3. **Changeset:** `@objectstack/spec` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset. Level and declarations are correct for a description change. I read each sentence against the code:
   - "said the switch gates only the Change Owner action": true of main's `.describe()`.
   - "also decides whether the offboarding hand-over … moves the object's `owner_id`": true.
   - "where the switch resolves off, those records are counted as held and keep their owner": **false on an ineligible object** (the must-fix).
   - "reads only the resolved on or off, not the per-record `visibleWhen`/`disabledWhen` predicates": true, the hand-over reads `.enabled` only.
   - "No shape, accepted value or default changes": true of the diff.
4. **Generated docs:** the one changed row of `object.mdx` equals the `.describe()` string, so it carries the same sentence and moves with the fix. `Skills-docs: none` holds: no file under `skills/` states what this switch gates.
5. **Sentences that hold:** the hand-over as a third reader of the one resolution; "single, bulk and cascade" for the action (unchanged text); "Gates the action and the hand-over's owner_id, not a plain owner_id write" (only `owner_id` takes `transfer_off`, other user fields are handed over); "It does not gate the raw write".
6. **Tests and gates:** the report's commands and outputs are real and pinned to this head (spec build and regen exit 0, `check:generated` 14 up to date, 253 tests, typecheck exit 0). No ablation is owed for prose. The six gates NOT MEASURED locally are all run by CI jobs on the PR: `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:doc-security-posture` and `check:skill-examples` in `Type Check · consumer gates`, `check:docs-transcript-drift` in `Type Check · workspace`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` in `Build Core`. Accepted as left to CI.

The fix push starts a new set, so this head's runs were not waited on.

- The comment above `export * from './user-action-transfer'` in `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts` on main still says the endpoint and the console action do not exist yet. It is outside this card and not in the diff.

Delta record by the reviewer of 7145492854, which found M1 on head 79e98ffc3b8. The new head is a merge of `origin/main` (e23a3a80315) plus two commits: the scoped sentences and the regenerated reference row. The whole diff against main was re-read, four files, and the three M1 sentences were read against the code again. Main moved nothing under `packages/core/src/security` or `packages/spec/src/data` between the two reads. Read-only shape: nothing was built or run.

Correction to the earlier record: it named the claim as 7145444800. The claim comment for that head is 7145451337.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The `.describe()` now carries the scope.** "On those objects it also decides whether the offboarding hand-over … moves owner_id" follows the sentence that defines where the action is offered (a platform-injected, provable, not read-only `owner_id`), which is `isTransferEligible`. That is the first half of `ownerTransferOff`.
